## Welcome back, divers {.section-break}

**Chapter 1 — Getting Started with Data in R**

Slides are a *scaffold*: one idea per slide, frequent retrieval check-ins, predict-then-check prompts. Click through and pause where you like.

## What you'll be able to do

By the end of this chapter, you will be able to:

- Distinguish between R (the language) and RStudio (the environment for using it)
- Install and load R packages from CRAN
- Explore a data frame using functions like `glimpse()` and `View()`
- Identify whether a variable is *categorical* or *quantitative*

::: {.predict}
Before we begin: which of these objectives feels least familiar to you right now? Hold that in mind — we'll check back at the end.
:::

## Check-in: What are R and RStudio?

::: {.predict}
Take 30 seconds. Predict your answer **before** clicking. Then tap your choice.
:::

::: {.mcq data-correct="b"}
<div class="mcq-stem">Q0. A colleague says they're 'opening Python in PyCharm to run the analysis.' By analogy, what's the equivalent claim in the R world?</div>
<ol class="mcq-options">
  <li>'Opening RStudio to use R-Studio'</li>
  <li>'Opening R in RStudio' — R is the language; RStudio is the IDE</li>
  <li>'Opening RStudio in R' — R is the IDE; RStudio is the language</li>
  <li>'Opening R in R' — they're the same thing</li>
</ol>
<div class="mcq-controls">
<button class="poll-btn show-poll">Show class poll</button>
<button class="show-answer">Show answer</button>
</div>
<div class="poll-bar"></div>
<div class="mcq-reveal"><strong>(b)</strong> R is to RStudio as Python is to PyCharm: the *language* runs inside an *integrated development environment* that makes writing and inspecting code more pleasant.</div>
:::

## Check-in: How do I code in R?

::: {.predict}
Take 30 seconds. Predict your answer **before** clicking. Then tap your choice.
:::

::: {.mcq data-correct="b"}
<div class="mcq-stem">Q0. An online store records each transaction's `order_id` as a five-digit number like `47291`. Should `order_id` be treated as numerical or categorical?</div>
<ol class="mcq-options">
  <li>Numerical, because the values are digits</li>
  <li>Categorical — it's an identifier, not a measurement; averaging two order IDs is nonsense</li>
  <li>Numerical, because you could compute the mean of the IDs</li>
  <li>Both — depends on context</li>
</ol>
<div class="mcq-controls">
<button class="poll-btn show-poll">Show class poll</button>
<button class="show-answer">Show answer</button>
</div>
<div class="poll-bar"></div>
<div class="mcq-reveal"><strong>(b)</strong> The test for *numerical* is whether arithmetic on the values is meaningful. Two order IDs don't add up to anything useful — they label distinct orders, just like ZIP codes label distinct postal regions.</div>
:::

## What are R packages? &mdash; key idea

**Instructor note:** anchor this section in one concrete example from the chapter (e.g., the `flights` data, a `ggplot` worked example, or a code chunk). One idea per slide; resist the urge to put the whole section on one screen.

## What are R packages? &mdash; live code

::: {.try-this}
Open RStudio (or paste into the book's webR block) and run the canonical example for this section. Ask one student to predict the output **before** running.
:::

```r
# Replace with the section's canonical code chunk.
library(moderndive)
library(tidyverse)

# e.g.,
# flights |> ggplot(aes(x = dep_delay)) + geom_histogram()
```

## Check-in: What are R packages?

::: {.predict}
Take 30 seconds. Predict your answer **before** clicking. Then tap your choice.
:::

::: {.mcq data-correct="b"}
<div class="mcq-stem">Q0. Last week you ran `install.packages('readr')` on your laptop. Today you reopen RStudio and want to use `read_csv()`. What do you need to do?</div>
<ol class="mcq-options">
  <li>Run `install.packages('readr')` again — installs reset between sessions</li>
  <li>Run `library(readr)` — the install persists across sessions, but the load doesn't</li>
  <li>Nothing — `read_csv()` is always available</li>
  <li>Type `read_csv()` and R will auto-load the package</li>
</ol>
<div class="mcq-controls">
<button class="poll-btn show-poll">Show class poll</button>
<button class="show-answer">Show answer</button>
</div>
<div class="poll-bar"></div>
<div class="mcq-reveal"><strong>(b)</strong> *Installing* puts the package on your machine (one-time). *Loading* with `library()` attaches it to your current R session (every session). This is why scripts often start with a block of `library()` calls.</div>
:::

## Check-in: Explore your first datasets

::: {.predict}
Take 30 seconds. Predict your answer **before** clicking. Then tap your choice.
:::

::: {.mcq data-correct="c"}
<div class="mcq-stem">Q0. Which of these object names will R **reject**?</div>
<ol class="mcq-options">
  <li>`student.grades`</li>
  <li>`studentGrades`</li>
  <li>`3rd_quarter_sales`</li>
  <li>`sales_q3`</li>
</ol>
<div class="mcq-controls">
<button class="poll-btn show-poll">Show class poll</button>
<button class="show-answer">Show answer</button>
</div>
<div class="poll-bar"></div>
<div class="mcq-reveal"><strong>(c)</strong> R object names can't start with a digit. `3rd_quarter_sales` errors at parse time; the others all start with a letter (or `.` followed by a non-digit) and are fine.</div>
:::
